DMV proxy service in Colorado

I take your documents to the DMV in person as your authorized agent, using Colorado form DR 2175 (Power of Attorney for Motor Vehicle Only), signed by the owner and notarized.

  1. The owner signs a DR 2175 naming me (or someone they trust).
  2. I notarize it, check the packet is complete, and submit it at the DMV.
  3. You get your receipts and documents back.

Frequently asked questions

Can a proxy submit my DMV paperwork in Colorado?

Yes. A vehicle owner can authorize another person to handle title and registration transactions with Colorado form DR 2175, Power of Attorney for Motor Vehicle Only. The owner signs it before a notary, and it expires on the date written on the form. With a notarized DR 2175 naming me, I submit your documents in person at the DMV. My standard proxy package typically totals $95–$165. You decide which forms to file; I don't give legal advice.

How much does bilingual DMV help cost in Denver?

Flat fees, confirmed in writing before we start: DMV form typing $55–$75, DMV proxy packages from $95, out-of-state title transfers typically $185–$245, and Colorado bonded title document prep $150. Government fees are paid separately.

Are your certified Spanish translations accepted by USCIS?

Each translation includes my signed certificate stating it is complete and accurate and that I am competent to translate Spanish to English, which is the format USCIS requests. The receiving agency always makes the final decision. Pricing: $30 first page, $25 each additional page.

Which areas do you serve?

The Denver Metro area from Loveland to Castle Rock: Denver, Adams, Arapahoe, Jefferson and Douglas counties, plus Broomfield and Longmont. I travel farther for a quoted fee, and bonded title prep is available remotely statewide.

How much does a notary public cost in Colorado?

Colorado caps the in-person notary fee at $15 per notarization. I charge $15, or $10 at a Community Hub. A mobile visit adds a travel fee (from $20) that is not set by state law and is always quoted in writing before the appointment.
